methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort (n=254) with pre-specified inclusion/exclusion criteria, consistent follow-up schedule, and multivariate Cox regression. The cutoff (GLR=11.71) was derived from the same cohort via maximum Youden index then applied to the same data, inflating apparent performance. Internal validation with 1000 bootstrap resamples (corrected C-index 0.772) partially mitigates overfitting but is not a substitute for external validation. Variables with P<0.1 in univariate were taken into multivariate (reasonable), and subgroup/interaction testing for GLR x tumor characteristics was performed. No sample-size calculation or formal consideration of competing risks for recurrence (22 non-recurrence deaths).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) of a simple, inexpensive lab-based biomarker with direct clinical applicability for NMIBC surveillance and adjuvant decision-making. The nomogram provides plausible incremental value (C-index 0.745 -> 0.785) but requires external validation before guideline integration. BCG utilization was only 4.3% (policy-driven), limiting generalizability to Western BCG-heavy settings.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic biomarker + nomogram study, REMARK (with TRIPOD elements) is appropriate. The manuscript provides detailed methods, patient flow diagram, baseline tables, multivariate Cox with HR/CI, calibration and DCA, and subgroup forest plot; these cover a reasonable subset of REMARK/TRIPOD items. Missing: no formal checklist, no reporting of missing-data handling, no pre-registration, no data or code availability, no external or multi-center validation cohort. Some writing redundancy (e.g., 'history of prior abdominal surgery as novel independent risk factor' restated twice in two consecutive sentences).

novelty_literature.justification: First evaluation of GLR specifically in NMIBC post-TURBt, extending prior work in other genitourinary and hepatic malignancies (pancreatic NETs, HCC, oral cancer, MIBC). The conceptual advance is incremental: GLR has been validated elsewhere and the analytical framework is standard (ROC cutoff, Cox regression, nomogram with DCA). Claim of superiority over NLR/PLR is supported by AUC difference (0.716 vs 0.552/0.535) but within a single cohort.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is readable and follows standard format. Discussion includes substantive mechanistic rationale for GGT and lymphocyte components. Some issues: duplicated passages (abdominal surgery hypothesis stated twice in close succession), Figure 5 legend mismatches subpanels (labels B and C referenced for '3-year (C) and 5-year (D)'), and Abstract states 3-year AUC of 0.72 consistent with Results but lists only that single value for nomogram discrimination. The sensitivity/specificity of the GLR cutoff (76.0/62.6) reveals modest discrimination that the text sometimes oversells.

key_strengths: First focused evaluation of GLR in NMIBC post-TURBt with multivariate Cox adjustment for size, number, grade, stage, and prior abdominal surgery
Inclusion of calibration curves, time-dependent ROC, and decision-curve analysis adds clinical decision context beyond raw discrimination metrics
Consistent prognostic effect of GLR across clinicopathological subgroups with formal interaction testing
Balanced distribution of adjuvant therapy between high/low GLR groups (P=0.844) reduces treatment-allocation confounding
key_concerns: Cutoff (GLR=11.71) derived and applied in the same cohort without external validation; internal bootstrap mitigates but does not replace this
BCG utilization only 4.3% (insurance-driven); findings may not generalize to BCG-rich practice settings
No competing-risks analysis despite 22 deaths during follow-up; OS vs RFS discrepancy handled only narratively
Duplicate text in Discussion ('history of prior abdominal surgery' rationale restated) and Figure 5 legend subpanel mismatch
No data/code availability statement or REMARK/TRIPOD checklist
Single-center retrospective design with inherent selection bias; external multicenter validation explicitly deferred
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent but narrowly scoped single-center prognostic biomarker study with incremental novelty and modest discrimination; appropriate for a lower-tier urology or oncology journal after minor revisions addressing figure legends, duplicated text, and reporting-standard gaps.
